card.profile: "El Vito" is a traditional folk song and dance music of Andalusia whose origins can be traced back to the 16th century. Its name refers to Saint Vitus, patron of dancers. It was created in the nineteenth century as a dancing song typical of the bolero. It includes steps in the art of bullfighting and is usually played by women. The typical costume includes jacket and brimmed hat.
card.insight: Folk duo Esther & Abi Ofarim recorded a version of "El Vito" for their 1967 album 2 in 3.
